pillar_reactions.evidence: Read the pillar back in his own terms to check he had it right: 'So you basically, he's basically making sure form and everything is right. And as far as things that some person may be struggling a little bit and prone to injury and cutting that stuff out.' He then returned twice to the question that actually mattered to him — 'how do I actually fit into this program?' and 'where would I fit in here?' — because with a kinesiology background he considered himself past the beginner stage. That question was answered with a Michael Jordan analogy rather than with a description of how the programme adapts to an experienced trainee.

No questions and no pushback. Notable for what it contains rather than his reaction: the pillar included fasting protocols delivered to a man who had disclosed type 2 diabetes twenty minutes earlier, with the rep tying it explicitly to his existing practice — 'You mentioned you do a good fast like once a year, you said? We're big on fasting too, especially as you enter our 50s, man. It's really important for longevity and health.' No dietary information was ever gathered from him, and no question was asked about medication.

The pillar the rep calls most important is the one this prospect explicitly rejected, and it is what lost the sale: 'I really wouldn't need [24/7 access]... if I just had something structured, like, okay, you do this, do this, and then we come back and we meet a month from now, we see where you at.' And again: 'I understand it's worth its value of gold, but I don't think I really need it. I don't really need that much.' Worth setting against what he had said in phase 4, unprompted — that the reason he has failed for 15 years is having no circle that holds him accountable. He named accountability as the root cause and then declined to buy it, and nobody connected the two.

anchors.raw: I saw something on his page. He was advertising the kettlebell routine in a PDF. What do you offer in that? You know what saying? And something like that, you know, structured workouts. $4,000, I don't need to spend that much money on it.
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own advertised PDF kettlebell routine
anchors.note: The most awkward anchor in the corpus because the competing product is the company's own marketing. The prospect had seen a cheap or free PDF routine advertised on Trevor's page and used it as the reference point for what he actually wanted. The direct question — 'What do you offer in that?' — was never answered on the call. If low-cost products are being advertised on the same channels that generate these calls, they are setting the price expectation before the closer speaks.

anchors.raw: I went to Penn State University for kinesiology, so I have a little exercise science background... I'm pretty much squared away with my limitations, my form, how to do things because I've done it before. I'm not a beginner on things.
anchors.note: A degree-level exercise science background is a strong undercut for a product priced on expert instruction, and the rep never found the counter — which was available and had been supplied by the prospect himself: fifteen years of knowing exactly what to do and not doing it. The one attempt, 'if you had the capability you would have done it', was rebutted immediately and correctly.

anchors.raw: I got a guy, one of my best friends, he owns a gym and he, but he's on like on the other side of town. So it's not really, you know what I mean?
anchors.competitor: A close friend who owns a gym
anchors.note: Free access to a gym and to a gym owner, disqualified only by geography. Mentioned inside his own answer about lacking an accountability circle, which makes it a partly self-defeating anchor and one the rep could have used — the friend has been available for fifteen years and has not moved the needle.

anchors.raw: We have something called Primal University. It's just 200 bucks, okay? You can cancel it at any time... you can either pay on a monthly basis or it's just two grand for the year.
anchors.note: Rep-created and, unusually in this batch, introduced only after the coaching had been genuinely declined on fit rather than to rescue a wavering close. Note two small inconsistencies: the rep says $200 while the checkout page shows $199, and the annual at $2,000 includes Trevor's live classes which the monthly does not — a differentiator the prospect had to discover by asking.

anchors.raw: I have a business. I have a business consulting business... I trade stocks. So some of the times I come in, I can do more research, figure out more streams of income
anchors.note: Amtrak employment plus a consulting business plus stock trading, and he confirmed he would have used a credit card had he wanted the programme. Affordability was never the obstacle here, which makes this the cleanest test in the batch of whether the offer can win on value alone. It could not.

unmet_demand.want: Structured programming without one-to-one supervision — a week-by-week plan he can execute alone, checked in on monthly rather than continuously
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The published ladder starts at $4,000 for three months of full-service coaching with no intermediate rung. The need was met only by Primal University, which was not mentioned until after the coaching had been refused and is not part of the published offer. Fourth prospect in three days to ask for exactly this.

unmet_demand.want: Nutrition guidance appropriate for diagnosed type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol, including whether fasting protocols are safe for him
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not established in any respect. The rep encouraged fasting without asking about medication, glucose management or who is treating him, and the prospect already fasts for 15 to 30 days at a time. He has now bought a product that includes nutrition advice with none of this resolved.

unmet_demand.want: Training that fits a midnight to 8am shift and a daily Philadelphia to New York commute
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised the logistics twice as the thing that attracted him and the answer was the generic 30-minutes-three-to-four-times-a-week framing. Nothing addressed shift rotation, training at 8am after a night shift, or the sleep disruption he had described.

unmet_demand.want: A direct answer about the PDF kettlebell routine advertised on Trevor's own page
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked outright and never answered. Whether that product exists, what it costs and how it relates to Primal University is apparently not something the closer can speak to, which leaves the company's own marketing competing with its offer unopposed.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that an experienced trainee with an exercise science degree gets something beyond beginner programming
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked 'where would I fit in here?' three separate times and received a Michael Jordan analogy rather than a description of how the programme scales for someone already competent. For a prospect whose whole objection is that he does not need the intensity, this was the question to answer.
